transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because... things have been pretty tough lately. Ever since they made me the acting workflow lead, I’ve been walking into the warehouse already tense. I find myself snapping over little SAP errors, and I'm missing cycle-count deadlines that I never used to miss. 

Then I go home and I'm just... I'm too drained to play basketball or even work on my sketches. It's just really getting to me, and I need to figure out how to get a handle on it.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
It's been... I'd say about four months now. It started right around the time they merged the inventory teams and actually put me in this acting workflow lead role.
Over these past four months, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless most days?
No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling down or hopeless like that. It's really just the stress and the frustration from work... I don't feel sad, just completely worn out and on edge all the time.
Aside from work, do you find yourself worrying excessively about other areas of your life, like your family, health, or finances?

No, not really. I mean, my family is fine, and I'm healthy enough. Finances are okay too. It's really just the job. When I'm not at the warehouse, I'm just too exhausted to worry about much else. The stress is pretty much all tied to this new role and the changes at work.

latest_inference.note: Ruled out F41.1 because excessive worry is confined strictly to the workplace stressor rather than multiple everyday domains.
